summary: Retested the VTO 'stuck timer' fix in frontend/src/pages/products/Fit.jsx (analysisFinished-listener + VTO_STUCK_TIMEOUT_MS toast) following up on iteration_9's finding. The fix WORKS as intended: the widget still visibly opens (~1s branded overlay) and still hangs internally forever on the vendor side (same expected/acceptable vendor-side hang, all network 200s, zero console errors) - but this time the toast 'The virtual try-on is taking longer than usual...' correctly fires at ~20s where it previously never fired at all. Verified across 3 separate runs with granular 2s-interval sampling. Clicking the trigger button a second time in the same session correctly re-arms a fresh 20s timer and produces a fresh toast again (~20-22s after the 2nd click), with zero new console errors/exceptions - confirmed via a detailed sampling run after an initial single-checkpoint run gave a false negative due to toast auto-dismiss timing in my own test script (not an app bug - resolved by sampling every 2s instead of one check at t=20s). Tab-switch regression (core->mobile->frame->core x2, 7 switches total) passed cleanly: 0 console errors, all fit-panel-* elements render on each switch, confirming the new analysisFinished useEffect doesn't break the persistent <tint-vto> element.
action_items: No action needed for this fix - toast-on-stuck behavior confirmed working. Underlying vendor SDK hang itself remains a live 3rd-party/vendor-side issue outside this codebase's control (per problem statement, this is expected/acceptable and not something to fix here).

Optional/minor: consider verifying the vendor's X close button inside the stuck overlay actually resets vtoLoading/timer state cleanly if clicked mid-hang (not explicitly re-tested this iteration; iteration_9 flagged it as untested too).
critical_code_review_comments: openVTO()'s widget.open().catch() handler shows a DIFFERENT toast ('couldn't open') and calls clearVtoStuckTimer() if open() rejects - this path was not exercised in this test (open() never rejected in any run), but is worth keeping in mind: if a future vendor update makes open() reject fast on repeat calls (e.g. 'already open' error) while the widget is still silently hung, the stuck-timer toast would be prematurely cancelled and replaced by the misleading 'couldn't open' toast instead. Low priority since not observed live.

The analysisFinished listener useEffect runs once on mount with an empty dependency array and does a one-time document.querySelector('tint-vto') - correct given the widget is a persistent singleton element per the existing comment in the file, and confirmed still valid across repeated opens/tab switches in this run.

success_rate.frontend: 100% - toast-on-stuck-timeout fix confirmed working, re-arm on 2nd click confirmed working, regression across tab switches clean, zero console errors throughout

context_for_next_testing_agent: This closes out the VTO toast-timing investigation from iteration_9. Confirmed via 3 playwright runs on https://kinetic-medtech-ui.preview.emergentagent.com/xofit-frame-fitting: (1) toast fires reliably at ~20s after clicking [data-testid='vto-trigger-button'] while widget is stuck, (2) clicking again re-arms and refires ~20s later, (3) 0 console errors across all runs, (4) tab-switch regression (fit-tab-core/mobile/frame, 7 switches) clean. IMPORTANT TESTING NOTE for future agents: when checking for the stuck-timer toast, sample every ~2s across the full window rather than a single check at exactly t=20s - sonner toasts auto-dismiss after a few seconds, so a single checkpoint can produce a false negative if it lands just after the toast already disappeared. The underlying vendor widget hang itself is unchanged/expected per the problem statement and is not a bug in this codebase.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - this iteration confirms the fix resolves the previously-identified gap (iteration_9's RCA: widget.open()'s promise resolves on overlay-mount, not true readiness). The new approach (arming a timer on open() and only clearing it via the vendor's 'analysisFinished' event) correctly surfaces the stuck state to the user instead of relying on the wrong promise signal.
